name: How do design-build firms coordinate architecture and construction on the same job?

mainEntity.name: How do design-build firms coordinate architecture and construction on the same job?
mainEntity.text: How do design-build firms coordinate architecture and construction on the same job?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coordination is the core of design-build. Instead of completing plans in isolation and hoping they fit the budget later, the design and construction teams work together from the start. That means architecture, engineering, pricing, and field input happen in parallel. The result is usually fewer surprises and a smoother transition from design to build. Homeowners should ask how often the team reviews constructability, who signs off on final drawings, and whether pricing is updated as the design progresses. In well-run projects, design choices are tested against budget and schedule continuously, not just at the end. That is what makes integrated delivery especially valuable for complex homes in Los Angeles.
acceptedAnswer.description: They coordinate architecture and construction through shared planning, regular review meetings, and continuous cost checks during design. That allows drawings to be adjusted before they become expensive changes in the field.
